newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank shares lead Beirut market upwards on week.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares lead Beirut market upwards on week.

text.p: Bank shares led the Beirut Stock Exchange upwards in the week ended on Friday amid heavy demand and expectations of further rises, brokers said.
The LIBX bank index rose 3.87 percent to 154.91. The LISPI general index rose 1.55 percent to 88.42 and the BLOM general index rose 1.08 percent to 940.94.
Turnover rose slightly to 1,135,002 shares from 1,074,511 last week but value dropped to $8,856,314 from $11,467,988.
Some 446,384 bank shares changed hands on demand of 992,801 and supply of 972,020.
Brokers said the three banks were rising on investor perceptions of stability and confidence fed by their good performance on the market since listing earlier this year.
Two of the three banks rose on the week. Bank of Beirut reached $3,937 from last week's $3.6785 after touching $4 on Tuesday.
"There is a good appetite for BOB shares, probably we will see them above $4," Ziad Makkawi of Middle East Capital Group told Reuters.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce hit a record high of $18.5 on Friday from last Friday's $17.75.
"It took BLC some time to establish investors confidence but it will go very well with an uptrend, especially if we consider that its Global Depositary Receipts are above $20," Makkawi said.
The BLC's GDR was $20-$20.4 on the London Stock Exchange on Friday.
Banque Audi held steady during the week at its all-time high of $23.125.
"I believe Audi is a top quality bank, it is a good stable investment," Makkawi said.
Solidere A and B shares also rose on heavy demand. A shares reached $10.625 from $10.5 and B shares rose to $10.875 from $10.75 after touching $11 on Thursday.
"Everybody is confident that Solidere shares are undervalued. They are 50 percent less than their value, so the performance is less than good," Makkawi said.
Of the four industrial shares, pipemaker Eternit climbed back to $2 from $1.9375 while Ciments Libanais was unchanged during the week at $1.28125.
There was no trade throughout the week in the other two listed firms Ciments Blancs and Uniceramic.
